newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares rise after debt rating, Gazprom.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares rise after debt rating, Gazprom.

text.p: Russian shares rose by more than one percent after ratings agencies assigned better-than-expected ratings to Russian debt, traders said on Monday.
The Russian Trading System 24-share index rose 1.32 percent to 163.51 on moderate volume of $11.54 million.
Prices of leading stocks rose after a generally flat and quiet day immediately after Standard & Poors, Moody's Investors Services and IBCA announced their ratings.
"After the news of the ratings came out, we are up 1-1.5 percent. We are seeing more buyers in the market," said Loren Bough, ADR trader at Brunswick Brokerage.
Bough said the ratings would enhance the credibility of Russia and were likely to bring more investors into equities.
S&P gave Russia a BB- long-term rating, Moody's set a Ba2 ceiling for long-term foreign currency bonds and IBCA gave it a BB+ long-term foreign currency rating.

"Undoubtedly, this is extremely positive news. Probably even better than expected," said Anton Kudryashov of Renaissance Capital. He added that the market had also taken support from the announcement earlier on Monday of the preliminary price for an issue of American Depositary Shares for Gazprom.
Lead managers Morgan Stanley and Dresdner Kleinwort Benson said each ADS, representing 10 ordinary shares, would be priced between $14 and $16.

"The combination of the ratings and a successful Gazprom deal at a reasonable price is a big credibility enhancer for the Russian market in the next two to three months and will help to negate the effects of (President Boris) Yeltsin's health problems," Bough said.
Yeltsin is awaiting heart surgery and the health issue has depressed shares in recent weeks.
Rostelekom rose to $2.37, from $2.30 on Friday, Unified Energy System rose to $0.0730 from $0.0718 and Mosenergo rose to $0.876 from $0.855.
